title: Bind every exposed frontend journey to an E2E or SMOKE browser spec

facts.note: Conventionally named browser specs are identifiable by path. Files under node_modules, dist, build or _generated are never scanned and never count as candidate specs.
A browser spec is also any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (// Train:, // Journey:, // URN: test:train:…, // URN: test:journey:…); needs a header-comment parser.
There is no established path convention for journey definitions; discovering journeys, whether their entrypoint is exposed, and their declared surfaces needs a journey-definition parser.

values: htmx_e2e_detector: exposed journey without E2E/SMOKE spec
facts.note: Detector cross-references every in-scope journey against // Journey: bindings and test URN kinds. Applies to all in-scope journeys at all times (new or pre-existing), not only to changed ones.

fires: A journey with an exposed entrypoint whose surfaces include frontend has no spec bound by // Journey: carrying an E2E or SMOKE test URN.
A journey with an exposed entrypoint that declares no surfaces has no bound E2E/SMOKE spec.
The only spec bound to an exposed frontend journey carries neither an E2E nor a SMOKE test URN.
An in-scope journey's only candidate spec lives under node_modules, dist, build or _generated: that file is ignored, so the journey has no qualifying spec outside excluded trees.
An in-scope journey is mentioned only by a unit test that names its URN in a string: that is not a browser spec, so the journey is still uncovered.
doesNotFire: The journey is internal (entrypoint not exposed).
The exposed journey's entrypoint surfaces exclude frontend (e.g. [backend]).
Files under node_modules, dist, build or _generated are themselves never scanned or judged.

given: A journey has an exposed entrypoint whose `surfaces` include `frontend` or declare none.
when: Always, for every such journey, new or existing (e.g. when the tester writes specs, or a journey is added or its exposure/surfaces change).
then: At least one browser spec MUST be bound to that journey with `// Journey: <journey id>` and carry an E2E or SMOKE test URN.
avoid: Counting a unit test that only mentions the journey URN in a string as coverage; it is not a browser spec and leaves the journey uncovered.
Relying on route-level tests alone: they prove each routing decision, not that the journey runs end to end in a browser.
Misnaming a spec to escape judgment: any test file with journey-marker header comments is judged as a browser spec.
unless: The journey is internal, or its exposed entrypoint `surfaces` exclude `frontend` (e.g. `[backend]`): no browser surface, out of scope.
Files in vendored/generated trees (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`) are never scanned (they neither are judged nor count as coverage).
why: An exposed journey is what a user can start. Route-level rules prove each routing decision; this rule proves the journey runs end to end in a browser.
evidence: For every exposed journey with frontend (or undeclared) surfaces, a spec file outside excluded trees exists with `// Journey: <journey id>` and an E2E or SMOKE test URN.
htmx_e2e_detector reports no findings for this rule.
verifier_detail: browser_spec = a `*.e2e.ts` file run by Playwright, OR any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`), so a misnamed one is still judged.
A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not a browser spec; it does not count as coverage and does not suppress a missing-coverage finding.
In scope: journeys whose entrypoint is exposed AND whose `surfaces` include `frontend` or declare no surfaces. Internal journeys and surfaces excluding `frontend` are out of scope.
Binding is via `// Journey:` header; qualifying test URN kinds are E2E or SMOKE.
Never scan `node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`; a candidate spec there is ignored, so a journey covered only there is reported as uncovered.
audit: New in the Bun/htmx browser tester, strict.
